paratext: explicit: cantibus gemmis Et tanquam Gloria patri et filio et spiritui sancto Et tanquam
bibliography: note(s): This item and the next are each written in different hands, both contemporary textura. Added after the explicit in bastard secretary, s. xv/xvi, is the note: ‘Ibo michi e The antems at mattyns and evynsong of saynt catheryne be two levys befor’ (i.e., at fol. 118v; the ‘Ibo michi’ direction refers to the text at fol. 112rv). This text answers the direction written in the upper margin of fol. 52v: ‘In þe fest of saynt Kateryn of sweth At procession Regnum mundi E and Induit me at the bokes ende’. In Syon 1, the antiphon added here appears at fols. 126v–7, written by the bastard secretary hand responsible for the added note here. De Hamel (1991:68–9) identifies the hand of CUL, MS Add. 8885 with that of Syon Abbey MS 6, fols. 3–136, and states that it is ‘very close’ to that of our MS and of BL, MS Harley 487 (a Psalter with other materials). Sotheby’s, London, 17 December 1991, catalogue 96 notes that ‘Thomas Raile was employed by the Abbess of Syon in 1482 for the writing and updating of the liturgical manuscripts at Syon, specifying that he was to write musical notes’; cf. Robert J. Whitwell, ‘An Ordinance for Syon Library, 1482’, English Historical Review 15 (1910), 121–3 and Mary C. Erler, ‘Syon Abbey’s Care for Books: its Sacristan’s Account Rolls for 1506/7–1535/6’, Scriptorium 39 (1985), 293–307. The cataloguer, de Hamel, thinks the Cambridge MS too early to be in Raile’s hand and the earliest of the surviving Syon processionals. But Raile’s could well be the bastard secretary hand which wrote the notes in the St John’s book and added texts in Syon 1.

bibliography: note(s): none corresponding to anything in Schneyer. The first five items begin: (i) Fol. 11: ‘Est filia melior filia ecclesciastici 36. Scimus sicut didicimus ab aristotele in liber de ’ (ii) Fol. 11v: ‘[a rubric in crayon: ‘Dominica in septuagesima] Petra autem erat cristus corinthiorum 10. cristus dicitur lapis siue petra hic et alibi ’ (iii) Fol. 12: ‘Fili recordare quod recepta beata In vita tua etc. Abraham vbi filium vocat ’ (iv) Fol. 12v: ‘Nostra conuersatio in celis est philippensium 3. set dicit quid eet esset celi dominio ’ (v) Fol. 12v: ‘Humilibus dat graciam etc. prou’ Est autem gracia ut donum gratuiter ’

A contents table, added later, in the concluding quire, fols. 220va–3ra ‘Iste collationes subscripte continentur superius in libro isto’, numbers the contents to 153 items (a marginal numeration imposed on the contents at that time). Most, but not all, are sermons, with a few short bits which appear to be exempla. None appear to be in Schneyer; incipits of the first five items are: (i) Fol. 25: ‘Videte quomodo caute ambuletis etc. Effesii 5. Scitis quod visus duo facit discernit ’ (ii) Fols. 25v–9: ‘Oculi sapientis in capite eius Ecclesiastice 7. In hiis illis 4. occurunt consideranda ’ (iii) Fols. 29–35v: ‘Numquid produces luciferum in tempore suo Iob 30. In his verbis prout competunt predicatori ’ A boundary with another text may have occurred on the lost leaf following fol. 32. (iv) Fols. 36–7: ‘Pater tenere diligit eum genesis 44. secundum Tullium amor est motus animi ’ (v) Fols. 37v–8v: ‘Exi a me quia homo peccator sum domine Luce 5. tanguntur 3a. potencie diuine confessio domine confitentis ’ At the end, fol. 223v is blank. The final leaves (fols. 224–5) are probably extraneous to the remainder, of s. xiv in. and covered with theological notes of various sorts, beginning with a fragment of a sermon, ‘Lingnum vite est hijs qui apprehenderunt eam 3a. sunt per quem sermocinantes frequenter animos attendunt ’ This scribe also adds material on blank leaves at the end of the next MS.

bibliography: note(s): (in Old English translation); The text begins imperfectly towards the end of bk. 1 at the word 'sume' (Miller 54/2). Bk. 2 begins on fol. 6r, bk. 3 on fol. 25 (the Interrogationes Augustini (Miller 64-88) occupying 9 leaves, fols 58r-66v, at the end of this book), bk. 4 on fol. 68r and bk. 5 on fol. 115v. Bk. 5 ends imperfectly at the word 'unwillsumlice' (Miller 442/23). Fol. 66v/18-27 and fol. 67r are blank. Fol. 2rv is missing, except for a small fragment. Single leaves missing after fols 5, 19, 24, 26, 86. (cf. Miller 56/14-58/29, 92/17-96/8, 134/1-136/18, 150/20-152/22, 158/23-162/10, 304/7-306/19. A passage in bk. 3 (Miller 206-8/4) is omitted as in CCCC 41. The scribe also omitted a long passage near the end of bk. 4, passing from ‘þæs ylcan myn[stres abbodesse]' (Miller 358/30), the closing words of fol. 104v, to [ðæs ilcan myn]stres abbod' (Miller 382/20), the opening words of fol. 115r. Later, s. x med., the missing text was added on ten leaves inserted after fol. 104r: it extended only to l. 19 on fol. 114v and in order to make an exact join the 23 lines on fol. 115r were erased (lines 24-29 were blank at the end of the book) and rewritten on fols 114v/19-115/21 in shorter lines. A continuous numeration of the chapters of bks. 1 and 2 has been erased, but numbers running from XI to XVIII in bk. 1 and from IX to XXI in bk. 2 can be made out and appear to be contemporary. The present chapter-numbers and the running titles were added in s. xiv and Latin glosses (fols 1r-7r, 58v-60r) and notes are also of this date. The name 'GODMÆR' is in the margin of fol. 83r.

Also includes Milburga (23 February) in red, Longinus (15 March), Joseph (19 March, added), Valeric of Leuconay (1 April and 12 December), Anselm (21 April, added, xii lessons), the discovery of St Denis (22 April), Neot (31 July, added), Dominic (5 August, added (?)) in red, Barloc (10 September), the conception of John the Baptist (24 September), Cybi (6 November) and Egwin of Evesham (30 December). Thomas Becket (29 December) is in red in the original hand (canonized 1173), whereas his translation (1220) is added (7 July). Obits of the abbots and benefactors of St Werburgh’s, Chester, added during the 14th, 15th and 16th centuries (published by Taylor, 1912). ‘O sapientia’ with neums (16 December). Notes on the number of hours in day and night, and verses on the ‘Egyptian’ days corresponding to Hennig’s (1955) set VIII. Astronomical notes and diagrams in medieval hands on pp. 3–5.

Incidentally some charters of Rombergh or Rumburgh, a Benedictine cell (fol. 35, cf. 132v) are included, and extracts from Court Rolls (in the case of copyhold tenants, fol. 70): and all is connected ultimately with the abbey of St. Mary at York. bibliography: note(s): Not known from any other sources. Everything after the opening lines of the summary of James is missing because of the loss of leaves. 2 Maccabees is missing because of a lacuna after fol. 150. Further lacunae in the summaries of Genesis (after fol. 1), 1 and 2 Chronicles (after fol. 21), 1 Maccabees (after fol. 150), Matthew (after fol. 153), 2 Thessalonians and 1 Timothy (after fol. 189) (see Collation). The order of books is that of the Later Version of the Wycliffite Bible, but includes 1 Ezra, Neemy, ‘ij Ezdre’ (i.e., 3 Ezra), and 4 Ezra subdivided into ‘iij Ezdre’ (4 Ezra, 1–2, in 6 chapters), ‘iiij Ezdre’ (4 Ezra, 3–14, in 34 chapters) and ‘v Ezdre’ (4 Ezra, 15–16, in 14 chapters) (see Ker (1960)). The summaries of Job, Proverbs and Ecclesiasticus are longer than average, and the summaries of Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezekiel are particularly long. Lamentations of Jeremiah appear as a separate item. The summaries of the gospels are short, whereas the summaries of 1–2 Corinthians and Hebrews are considerably longer than average. Commentary, most attributed to Lyra, appears in psalms and occasionally in other summaries. Agrees in wording with both the Earlier Version of the Wycliffite Bible and the Later Version of the Wycliffite Bible, but is largely independent and is not particularly close to either.; Psalms are individually summarised, with entries largely consisting of commentary attributed to Lyra and the Glossa Ordinaria. The entries are preceded by Latin incipits. Larger initials at psalms 26, 38, 52, 68, 80 and 109. Psalm numbers in Arabic numerals are written in the margins by the main scribe.; Running titles in brown ink, in English or Latin, on both rectos and versos consisting of abbreviated titles of biblical books. Chapter numbers as Arabic numerals in the margins. Large spaces corresponding to 3–10 lines of text are left blank between the summaries of individual books, presumably intended for rubrics but not filled in.

bibliography: note(s): Chapters XII-XLVI and LXIIII of the cartulary, printed in Brewer and Martin, i. 277-278, from PRO, E 164/24. See also the notes in vol. ii, p. xxix; Opens with a list of knights owing service to the abbey, which may have been an addition in the exemplar; The majority of the charters, which are arranged in an approximately chronological order, are royal grants cast directly in favour of the abbey. They thus create the impression of an uninterrupted process of endowment, beginning in the last quarter of the seventh century and extending throughout the eighth, ninth and tenth centuries, and culminating with Edward the Confessor’s general confirmation of lands (dated 1065). The series does, however, also include a related group of texts of more varied import, representing the abbey’s dealings with Ealdorman Ordlaf in the early tenth century, and one charter, in the name of King Æthelred, cast straightforwardly in favour of a layman (Kemble: The Anglo-Saxon Charters Website); The cartulary concludes with a Latin document purporting to be a bull of Pope Sergius I for Aldhelm and Malmesbury abbey. (For the suggestion that the Latin is a translation of an Old English text, itself adapted from an authentic papal bull in Latin, see Heather Edwards, 'Two Documents', Historical Research 139 [1986], pp. 9-15)

paratext: incipit: Nox precessit dies autem appropiabit. abiciamus ergo opera tenebrarum et induamur arma lucis. (Rom. 13.12) Primus aduentus sponsi qui est rex regum et dominus dominancium a prophetis et patriarchis prenunciatus est. qui quasi precursores et prenuncii extiterunt matrimonii inter cristum et ecclesiam
paratext: explicit: qui et lux et dies est qui pro nobis dignatus est nube carnis indui qui cum patre et filio et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat deus per omnia secula seculorum Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): De aduentu domini. primus.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217; Canterbury, Cathedral Library, MS. lit. B. 13; Salisbury, Cathedral Library, MS. 97.

paratext: incipit: Tu exsurgens misereberis syon⹎ quia tempus miserendi eius quia uenit tempus. (Ps. 101.14) In patre unitas. in filio⹎ in filio equalitas. in spiritu sancto unitatis equalitatisque connexio.
paratext: explicit: ad delicias eterne iocunditatis ad quas nos perducat ille qui pro nobis factus est temporalis. qui cum patre et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat deus per omnia secula seculorum Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): ·iiꝰ· Quare filius sit incarnatus.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217; Cambridge, Peterhouse, MS. 255; Canterbury, Cathedral Library, MS. lit. B. 13; and Oxford, Merton College, MS. 180, fols. 159r–162v (under the rubric Alexander in primo aduentu scolaribus Oxonie).

paratext: incipit: Et tu turris gregis nebulosa filie sion usque ad te ueniet. et ueniet prima potestas regnum filie ierusalem. (Mich. 4.8) Vulgo notum est tres esse aduentus saluatoris. Primus erat in carne. Secundus erat ad iudicium. Tercius in corde fidelis hominis.
paratext: explicit: uere delicie⹎ ad quas nos perducat ille. qui est turris fortitudinis qui cum patre et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat deus per omnia secula seculorum Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Tercius de aduentu.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Canterbury, Cathedral Library, MS. lit. B. 13; Salisbury, Cathedral Library, MS. 97.

paratext: incipit: Cum natus esset ihesus in bethleem iude in diebus herodis regis. Ecce magi ab oriente uenerunt ierosolymam dicentes. ubi est qui natus est rex iudeorum? (Matth. 2.1) In archa federis non solum manna erat appositum sed eciam uirga. Quia in sancta ecclesia non solum desideratur manna dulcedinis eloquii diuini
paratext: explicit: cum rege nostro conregnemus eternaliter. Quod nobis prestare dignetur qui in eternum regnabitur et ultera. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): In Epyphania domini.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217 and Cambridge, Peterhouse, MS. 255.

paratext: incipit: Nunc dimittis seruum tuum domine secundum uerbum tuum in pace quia uiderunt oculi mei salutare tuum quod parasti ante faciem omnium populorum lumen ad revelacionem gencium et gloriam plebis tue israhel. (Luc. 2.29) Mel deo non offerebatur. sed in omni sacrificio necessarius est usus salis.
paratext: explicit: nec in cor hominis ascendit quam nobis prestare dignetur qui uiuit et regnat per omnia secula seculorum Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): In purificacione beate marie.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217.

paratext: incipit: Memento queso sicut lutum feceris me. et in puluerem reduces me. (Job 10.9) Qui de terra est de terra loquitur. Qui lutum est de luto loquitur.
paratext: explicit: Hec mutatio est miraculo dextere excelsi. Ad quam nos perducat qui cum patre et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat deus per omnia secula seculorum Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo ·iꝰ· in capite ieiunii.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217.

paratext: incipit: Filia decepisti me. sed et tu ipsa decepta es. (Jud. 11.35) Postulatis instanter a me ut uerba proponam penetrancia in modum teli spiritualiter ad medullam cordis.
paratext: explicit: nisi uiolenti diripiunt regnum dei. ad quod nos perducat quia pro nobis passus est. Qui pro nobis carnem suam optulit. Qui cum patre et spiritu sancto etc.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo ·2ꝰ· in capite ieiunii.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217; Canterbury, Cathedral Library, MS. lit. B. 13; and London, British Library, Harley MS. 325.

paratext: incipit: Dulce lumen et delectabile oculis uidere solem. (Eccli. 11.7) Qui detinentur lecto doloris appropinquante die saltem aliquo reficiuntur solacio.
paratext: explicit: Ad hanc comprehensionem perducat nos ille qui est uera lux. Qui cum patre et spiritu sancto etc. Amen.
bibliography: note(s): Also in MS. Hatton 102, fol. 135r–v; Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217; and Cambridge, Peterhouse, MS. 255, fols. 159r–v.

paratext: incipit: Letare ierusalem et conuentum facite omnes qui diligitis eam. Gaudete cum leticia qui in tristicia fuistis. ut exultetis et saciemini ab uberibus consolacionis uestre. (Cantus g00776) Septuaginta annis detinebantur filii israel in captiuitate babilonica. et ideo septuaginta⹎ quod septuagies peccauerant
paratext: explicit: ab ubertate consolacionis uestre. ad quam consolacionem nos perducere dignetur iesus cristus. Qui cum patre et spiritu sancto amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Dominica ·4ª· 40º sermo.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217.

paratext: incipit: Abraham mortuus est et prophete mortui sunt. Et tu dicis si quis seruauerit sermones meos mortem non gustabit in eternum⹎ Respondit ihesus. dicitis. abraham pater uester exultauit ut uideret diem meum. uidit et gauisus est. (John 8.52) Homo mortalis de morte loquitur. mortalis et moritur. immo iam ex parte mortuus. talis materia tales decet⹎ quales nos sumus.
paratext: explicit: inenarrabili. gaudio eterno. Ad quod nos perducat ihesus cristus. qui cum patre spiritu sancto etc. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in dominica 4ª 40º.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217.

paratext: incipit: Transeamus usque bethlehem⹎ et uideamus hoc uerbum quod factum est. (Luc. 2.15) In ortu uere leticie. in natiuitate illius qui est uera leticia⹎ letari nos decet
paratext: explicit: uideamus eternaliter saluatorem nostrum. fratrem nostrum. qui factus est pro nobis homo. Qui cum patre et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat deus per omnia secula seculorum. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): In die Natalis domini.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217; Oxford, Merton College, MS. 180, fols. 159r–162v; Salisbury, Cathedral Library, MS. 97.

paratext: incipit: Filii hominum usquequo graui corde. ut quid diligitis uanitatem et queritis mendacium. (Ps. 4.3) Qui solet ante homines disercior esse⹎ facundus minus est cum uenit ante deos. Vos autem dii estis.
paratext: explicit: adiutor noster. spes nostra ihesus cristus. Qui cum patre et spiritu sancto etc.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in sinodo.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217.

paratext: incipit: Cum uenit plenitudo temporis misit deus filium suum factum ex muliere. factum sub lege ut eos qui sub lege erant redimeret ut adoptionem filiorum reciperemus. (Gal. 4.4) Post longam uatum seriem. post tantam prophetarum et patriarcharum expectacionem. post longa gemencium suspiria⹎ uenit expectatus. uenit desideratus gentibus.
paratext: explicit: deliciis eterne iocunditatis eternaliter fruentur. Ad quas nos perducat ille qui cum patre et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat deus per omnia secula seculorum. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in festo circumcisionis ihesu cristi.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217 and Oxford, Merton College, MS. 180, fols. 159r–162v.

paratext: incipit: Vbi est. qui natus est rex iudeorum? (Matth. 2.4) Fluuius egrediebatur de loco uoluptatis. in iiiiºʳ flumina diuisus. Nomen uni⹎ tigris. nomen secundo⹎ erat eufrates. Nomen tercio⹎ phison. Quarto⹎ geon. Tigris⹎ uelocitas. euphrates⹎ frugifer. phison⹎ mutacio oris. geon⹎ interpretatur hiatus terre.
paratext: explicit: Ecce quonammodo adimpletur quod scribitur.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in Epiphania domini nostri ihesu cristi.
bibliography: note(s): Fol. 41 is mostly torn away, resulting in the loss of the close of this sermon and the opening of the next.; Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217; Salisbury, Cathedral Library, MS. 97.

paratext: incipit: Nec sicut egreditur in nobis⹎ nisi nos ingressus fuerit.
paratext: explicit: magna est fides propter fructum magnum. quia ei debetur gaudium quod nec oculus uidit. nec audis audiuit. nec in cor homo ascendit. Quod nobis prestare dignetur. Qui cum patre et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat. Amen.
bibliography: note(s): Opening lost; the contents list (fol. xvi) lists the opening quotation as Egressus ihesus secessit in partes tyri et sidonis et ecce mulier (Matt. 15.21).

paratext: incipit: Si obliti sumus nomen dei nostri et si expandimus manus nostras ad deum alienum⹎ Nonne deus requiret ista? ipse enim nouit abscondita cordis. (Ps. 43.21) Qui percusserit cariatsepher dabo illi axam filiam meam uxorem. cepitque eam atoniel. suspirauitque ut sedebat asino axa. cui caleph. Quid habes inquid. at illa. terram arentem dedisti mihi⹎ iunge et irriguam. dedit ei caleph irriguum superius et inferius. (Ios. 15.16–19) Historiam cum allegoria et anagoge omittentes⹎ tropologie deseruiamus. hec enim uos precipue decet.
paratext: explicit: qui peccata nostra portauit. Qui cum patre et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat per omnia secula seculorum. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in sinodo.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217 and London, British Library, Harley MS. 325.

paratext: incipit: Hii sunt uiri misericordie qui assistunt dominatori uniuerse terre. (Eccli. 44.10) uel ut habet alia translatco. Hii sunt duo filii olei. qui etc. Preclara sollempnitas lucis hodierne ad spirituales delicias interne iocunditatis nos inuitat.
paratext: explicit: Vt opitulantibus meritis eorum filii misericordie meresmur effici. et assistere dominatori uniuerse terre. Quod ipse prestare dignetur etc.
paratext: rubric(s): Semo in festo sanctorum apostolorum Petri et Pauli.
bibliography: note(s): Also in MS. Lyell 8, fol. 119v; Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217.

paratext: incipit: Ad locum unde exeunt flumina reuertuntur. ut iterum fluant. (Eccle. 1.7) Multipliciter exercitatur desidia nostra nisi dissimulare uelimus. Reducere possumus ad memoriam peccata primorum parentum.
paratext: explicit: perueniamus ad pacem eternitatis. Quod nobis prestare dignetur qui cum patre et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat deus per omnia secula seculorum. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in festo sancte Marie Magdalene.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217.

paratext: incipit: Que est ista que ascendit de deserto deliciis affluens in nixa super dilectum suum? (Cant. 8.5) Spicas licet legere post manus messorum booz.
paratext: explicit: Vt quo precessit delibacio⹎ sequatur et massa quod nobis prestare dignetur qui cum patre et spiritu etc. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in assumpcione beate marie.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217; Cambridge, Peterhouse, MS. 255, fols. 157v–158r; and Canterbury, Cathedral Library, MS. lit. B. 13.

paratext: incipit: Venit mater salomonis ad regem salomon. Surrexitque rex in occursum eius. adorauitque eam. et sedit super thronum suum. positusque thronus matris que sederit sedit ad dexteram eius. Dixitque. Vnam rem parvulam a te peto. ne confundas faciem meam. Et dicit rex. pete mater mea. neque fas est ut auertam faciem tuam. (3 Reg. 2.19) Gloriosa dicta sunt de te. ciuitas Dei. scilicet beata uirgo. in qua mansit ad tempus cristus secundum carnem.
paratext: explicit: et ad uitam perducat eternum. Quam nobis prestare dignetur qui cum patre et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat deus per omnia secula seculorum. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in die assumpcionis gloriose marie uirginis.

paratext: incipit: Terra erat inanis et uacua. et tenebre erant super faciem abyssi. et spiritus dei ferebatur super aquas. Dixitque deus fiat lux. et facta est lux. Et uidit deus lucem quod esset bona. et diuisit lucem a tenebris. Applauitque lucem diem. et tenebras noctem. factumque est uespere et mane dies unus. (Gen. 1.2) Natiuitatis gloriose uirginis marie preclara sollempnitas⹎ ad spirituales delicicas iocunditatis interne nos inuitat.
paratext: explicit: quo eternaliter fruentur filii lucis permansuri in eternis deliciis iocunditatis eterne. Quam nobis prestare dignetur. Qui cum patre et spiritu uiuit etc.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in festo natiuitatis sancte marie uirginis.

paratext: incipit: Omnia tempus habent et suis spaciis transeunt uniuersa sub sole. Tempus est nascendi. tempus moriendi tempus scindendi. consuendi. tempus est belli. tempus est pacis. (Eccle. 3.1) Spice relicte sunt legentibus post manus messorum booz. Alius est qui metit. Alius qui seminat. (John 4.37) Apostoli enim messuerunt que non seminauerunt.
paratext: explicit: tunc habetis pacem qui modo bella sustinetis quam nobis dignetur. Qui cum patre et spiritu sancto etc. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo ad Cistercienses.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217, fols. 146r–147v (Sermo ad monachos Cisterciensis) and London, British Library, Harley MS. 325.

paratext: incipit: Super flumina babilonis illic sedimus et fleuimus cum recordaremur syon. (Ps. 136.1) In salo huius mundi uera non potest esse securitas.
paratext: explicit: patriam queramus. supernam sion matrem nostram. Ad quam nos perducat ihesus cristus. dominus noster. Qui cum patre et spiritus sancto etc.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in lxxª
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217; Salisbury, Cathedral Library, MS. 97.

paratext: incipit: Dabo uobis cor carneum. (Ez. 36.26) Cor nostrum cristus est de quo dicit sponsa. languens amore. Ego dormio et cor meum uigilat. (Cant. 2.5) Dum igitur dormimus per contemplacionem⹎ uigilat cor nostrum cristus
paratext: explicit: ut nos recipiat in eterna tabernacula. quod ipse prestare dignetur qui cum deo patre. et spiritu sancto. uiuit et regnat deus per omnia secula seculorum. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in annunciacione dominica.

paratext: incipit: Quem queritis? An ihesum queritis nazarenum crucifixum? surrexit non est hic. set ite et dicite discipulis eius et petro. quoniam precedit uos in galileam. ibi eum uidebitis sicut dixit uobis. (Marc. 16.6) Ad uesperum demoratus est fletus. demoretur igitur ad matutinum leticia⹎ iocunditatis spiritualis.
paratext: explicit: ibi eum uidebitis sicut dixit uobis. Quod ipse prestare dignetur qui cum patre et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat deus per omnia secula seculorum. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in die Pentecost’ Pasche.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Canterbury, Cathedral Library, MS. lit. B. 13; London, British Library, Harley MS. 325; Salisbury, Cathedral Library, MS. 97.

paratext: incipit: Venit hora et nunc est etc. (John 4.23) Verba que ego loquor spiritus et uita sunt. (John 6.64) quia satis innuunt nobis illum esse amandum per quem sumus.
paratext: explicit: Assumpsit humanum contulit diuinum etc.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo de cristi parasceue. Vel in die palmarum.
bibliography: note(s): Part of fol. 72 torn away.

paratext: incipit: Necessitas moriendi fuit in cristo. non exactione superans animum sed ex uoluntate assringens euentum.
paratext: explicit: dare. uel contristare.

paratext: incipit: Cum appropinquaret ihesus ierosolimam uidens ciuitatem fleuit super illam. dicens. si cognouisses et tu. (Luc. 19.41) Ciues oxonie uiri dulcissime conuersationis ad longe maiorem morum honestorum obseruanciam tenentur. quam ceteri ciues regionis istius. maximum enim temporis spacium euolutum est.
paratext: explicit: in qua erimus ciues summi imperatoris ad quam nos perducat ihesus cristus qui cum patre et spiritu sancto etc. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in dominica xª post festum trinitatis.
bibliography: note(s): Addressed to the people of Oxford.; Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217.

paratext: incipit: Erat titulus cause inscriptus. Hec est ihesus nazarenus rex iudeorum. (Marc. 15.26) In sacro tempore huius sacratissimi ieiunii seria proponere decet uiris grauibus.
paratext: explicit: Venite benedicti. percipite regnum. quod nobis prestare dignetur qui etc. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in die parasceue.
bibliography: note(s): Also in London, British Library, Harley MS. 325.; Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217 and Canterbury, Cathedral Library, MS. lit. B. 13.

paratext: incipit: Ponam tabernaculum meum in medio uestri⹎ et non abiciet uos anima mea. ambulabo inter uos et ero deus uester. (Lev. 26.11) Dominus deus noster loquens populo suo peculiari. inuitans illum ad obseruancias preceptorum⹎
paratext: explicit: sufficiencia omnium. Ad hanc sufficienciam nos perducat qui carnem pro nobis assumere dignatus est ihesus cristus dominus noster. Qui cum patre et spiritu etc. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Sermo in annunciacione dominica.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, University Library, MS. Ii.1.24, fols. 141r–142vb.

paratext: incipit: Obsecro uos tamquam aduenas et peregrinos abstinere uos a carnalibus desideriis que militant aduersus animam. (1 Petr. 2.11) Tam ea que geruntur in sancta ecclesia. quam ea que exterius sensibus occurrunt⹎ instruunt nos et inuitant ad debitam intelligenciam nisi dissimulare uelimus.
paratext: explicit: ciues nos effecturus superne ierusalem patrie nostre. quod prestare dignetur qui cum patre et spiritu sancto etc. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Dominica 2ª post oct’ pasche sermo.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS. 217.

paratext: incipit: Ego sum pastor bonus. pastor animam suam ponat pro ouibus suis. (John 10.11) Imperfectum meum uiderunt oculi mei. (Ps. 138.16) Statum ergo imperfeccionis mee et imperfeccionem status mei recolligens uiris religiosis quorum conuersacio in celis est qui cum iocob lapidem capitibus suis supposuerunt predicare reformido.
paratext: explicit: non ad sinistram cum edis. Quod nobis prestare dignetur. qui cum patre et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat deus per omnia secula seculorum. Amen.
paratext: rubric(s): Dominica ·1· post oct’ pasche sermo.
bibliography: note(s): Also in Salisbury, Cathedral Library, MS. 97.

work: title: New Testament in the Later Version of the Wycliffite Bible
work: standard title(s): Bible, New Testament (later Wycliffite version) [Middle English]
bibliography: note(s): [item 2 occupies quires II–XVII]; With usual prologues and usual rubrics in black preceded by red paraphs (e.g., Here begynneþ a prologe on matheu; Ierom in hise twey prologis on matheu seiþ pleynly þus). John ends three-quarters down the first column on fol. 60v, the rest of the column is left blank and the prologue to Romans starts at the beginning of the second column on the same page. Running titles on both rectos and verses, in black ink preceded by red paraphs. Chapters have two numbers up to fol. 76r: one in black ink in the hand of the main scribe, consisting of an abbreviated capitulum usually followed by an Arabic numeral, another in red ink with c(apitulu) m usually followed by a Roman numeral; both are preceded by a single large red paraph. Chapters after fol. 76r have a single number, usually in black ink.; Red paraphs are sometimes used to mark units within the text, such as the beginnings of parables on fol. 12r. Corrections in the margins in a contemporary hand and over erasures within the text. No marginal glosses; added material within the text is occasionally underlined in red; lections are not marked. Nota written in the margins in a medieval (?) hand mark the following passages: Luke 11 (a woman of þe company reride hir voice & seide to him blessid be þe wombe…, fol. 39r); Ephesians 4 (to ech of us grace is ȝouun by þe mesure of þe ȝiuyng of christ…, fol. 80r); Acts 13 (y haue foundun dauiþ þe sone of iesse a man after myn herte…, fol. 102v); Apocalypse 2 (þat haþ iȝen as flawme of fier & hise feet lijk latoun…, fol. 120r); Apocalypse 20 (& whane a þousinde ȝeeris schulen be endid sathanas schal be vnboundun of his prisoun…, fol. 126v). At the end Here endiþ apocalips of John in the original hand, followed by an addition in a contemporary hand: what is softer þan christes ȝok & liȝter þen christes charge. þat is a mon to be proued in al þinges. abstene fro trespas. to wilne good. not wilne yuel. to loue al men. haten noon. to geten euerlastyng þynges. to be not taken or disseyued bi temperal þinges. to wilne not to do an oþer man þat þat is heuy or greuous to hym selff to suffre.

Texts in two columns in two 13th-century cursive hands. The first column contains a medical excerpt (or excerpts (?)) beginning ‘Duobus namque modis inueteratur homo ...’. The second column has copies of two 13th-century York ecclesiastical records: the first is a letter of prior frater Johannes to the archbishop of York; the other concerns the church of ‘Boneye’ in the diocese of York.

Psalms [1]–150, without titles or numbers, written with each verse starting on a new line. Punctuated throughout, with punctus used to mark the ends of verses, punctus elevatus used to mark metrum, and punctus or punctus elevatus used to mark minor pauses. Imperfect at the beginning because of a missing leaf, starting at 2: 3. The following text is also missing, because leaves, mainly those which used to contain initials at the ten-fold textual divisions, were cut out: – pp. 42b–42c are a fragment (missing text 24: 21–26: 2); – four leaves missing after p. 82 (missing text 42: 5–46: 8); – one leaf missing after p. 92 (missing text 51–52: 2); – a quire missing after p. 146 (missing text 77: 9–81: 8); – one leaf missing after p. 176 (missing text 96: 5–97: 5). Initials were also cut out, with the loss of the surrounding text, at the beginning of psalms 38 (pp. 73–74), 68 (pp. 121–122), 101 (pp. 181–182) and 109 (pp. 213–214). The opening lines of psalm 109, partially preserved, are written in large capitals in alternating red, green and blue ink. Originally there may have been decorated initials at psalms 26, 38, 51, 52, 68, 80, 97, 101 and 109. Subdivisions within psalms are not marked, apart from 17: 26 (fol. 26v); psalm 118 is subdivided into a mixture of 8-verse and 16-verse units (118: 41, 118: 73, 118: 89, 118: 121, 118: 137, 118: 153 and 118: 169 are not marked by larger initials). Psalms 148–150 are written as a single text. Two 14th-century hands added in margins, at the beginning of many psalms, the opening words of antiphons for the use of York, many with musical notation. Pp. 231–232 and 247–248 are repaired with parchment and missing words are supplied in a 14th-century (?) hand.

Calendar, laid out one month per page, written in black, red, blue and green, not graded, approximately two-thirds full. Only red and black are used on fols. 5v–6v (October–December). ‘Caput draconis anno domini M . cc . viijo ciclo xixii . xiiio’ (13 January). Includes Bercthum (14 May), the first abbot of Beverley Minster (‘Sancti Bricthuni abbatis’) in red, Cuthbert (20 March) and his translation (4 September), Benedict (21 March) and his translation (11 July), John of Beverley (7 May) with octave, Dunstan (19 May), the nativity of John the Baptist (24 June), his conception (26 September) and martyrdom (29 August), Oswald (5 August) and his translation (14 April), the translation of Hilda (25 August), and Martin (11 November and 4 July), all in red, blue or green. Many notes and obits added in late 13th-century hands, including ‘Atheline de shep(eie)’ (29 April), ‘Galfridi de shepeie’ (29 June) and ‘helyanore de grey’ (17 August). Dates of battles of 1455–1485 added in 15th-century hands. The months are headed by verses on the ‘Egyptian’ days which correspond to Hennig’s (1955) sets III and I (June) and notes on the lengths of the solar and lunar months. The months are followed by notes on the number of hours in day and night.

bibliography: note(s): (with the Glossa ordinaria of Franciscus Accursius); Two complete leaves from the same manuscript, with part of book two of Justinian’s Institutiones, framed by the Glossa ordinaria of Franciscus Accursius (d. 1260). For Accursius and the Glossa ordinaria, see Dondorp and Schrage, pp. 23‒25.; The gloss is that printed, with only minor variations, in the 1468 edition of Justinianus, Institutiones [with the Glossa ordinaria of Accursius], for which we have consulted Bod-Inc. J‒230 (Oxford, Bodleian Library, Auct. 4Q 2.1). Only one side of each fragment is visible as the leaves remain pasted to the boards. The left-hand margin of Fragm. II (approximately 4 mm), which formerly formed a hook round the last quire of the De animalibus, is now lost, with the result that in each line of the gloss the first few letters are missing. ; Interlinear and occasional marginal glosses in several hands. The interlinear glosses, mostly in Fragm. II, and one marginal note are contemporary with the text hand, whereas an Isaiah quotation (5:12) and Latin verses (Pronaque cum spectant … (Ovid, Metamorphoses, 1.84‒87), and Collige natura que perveniunt sine cura Messes cultura lac lanum collige cura, unidentified) in Fragm. I are in distinctive late-medieval English hands, most likely added after the leaf was used in this binding. The two-line note at the foot of Fragm. II (Versus [:] Mutuo dat nummos ..., with a definition of Alienacio), also in a distinctive English hand, may be an earlier addition. These hands are similar in character (although not identical) to those of the early 16th-century marginal notes that run throughout the two parts of the incunable Sammelband.; The leaves are incorrectly identified in Bod-Inc.
